solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Island commander sports angry wound

indicators.note: to sport something is to wear it, so the angry wound wears the commander inside it

parts.note: angry means mad
a wound leaves a scar
an aga is a Turkish military commander

explanation.surface: A furious officer is shown off with a nasty injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' means wears, so the angry wound wears the commander inside it. An aga was a Turkish officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Indian Ocean island nation off the east coast of Africa.

clue.text: Old farmer's waterproof put on sick lad

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
to don clothes is to put them on

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters of lad are in a bad way and rearranged

explanation.surface: An old farmer's raincoat is draped over an ill boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'farmer' stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay. 'sick' rearranges LAD into ALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Old MacDonald had a farm, in the nursery song, so he is the old farmer.

clue.text: Sheridan version features sinister housekeeper

indicators.note: features says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A production of a Sheridan play includes a menacing servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheridan was an 18th-century playwright, which makes 'version' look like a stage adaptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Danvers is the menacing housekeeper of Manderley in Daphne du Maurier's novel Rebecca.

clue.text: Artist comes up with sensible framework

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a mature person is sensible

explanation.surface: A painter arrives with a level-headed structure for a work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns RA into AR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An armature is the supporting skeleton inside a sculpture, or the frame of a motor's coil.

clue.text: Church and priest hail new sect member

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A church and its priest greet a newcomer to a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges AND PRIEST HAIL into RISTADELPHIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Christadelphians are a small Christian denomination founded in the nineteenth century, so one adherent fits.

clue.text: Kid left an overcoat

parts.note: to kid someone is to rag or tease them

explanation.surface: A child abandoned a winter coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child but is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A raglan is a loose overcoat with sleeves running to the collar, named after Lord Raglan.

clue.text: God shows an interest? Not at first!

indicators.note: the opening letter is dropped from the word for showing an interest

parts.note: someone who cares shows an interest

explanation.surface: A deity takes notice, though not straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' removes C from CARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war, counterpart of the Roman Mars.

clue.text: Stagger endlessly on in surrounding area of rainforest

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for stagger is cut off

parts.note: to stagger someone is to amaze them

indicators.note: surrounding has in wrapped round the letter for area

explanation.surface: Someone lurches on and on round a patch of jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the stagger word; 'surrounding' wraps 'in' round the area letter. 'of rainforest' is an adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South American rainforest is the Amazon, so the adjective describes things belonging to it.

clue.text: Writer's the writer powerless character inspires

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the character takes the writer inside
powerless removes the letter standing for power

parts.note: a character in a story is a person
the writer of a clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: An author is inspired by a feeble character.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Writer' means 'is'. 'powerless' drops P (power); 'inspires', literally breathing in, takes the writer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist and poet of transcendentalism.

clue.text: One taking in study connected with old Babylonian region

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
Sumer was the ancient region of southern Mesopotamia, later part of Babylonia

explanation.surface: A scholar researching ancient Mesopotamia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One taking in' is consuming, as one takes in food.
explanation.definitionFit: A consumer is someone who eats, uses or absorbs things, taking them in.

clue.text: Attack same point twice that's on chin

parts.note: to go at someone is to attack them

indicators.note: twice says the point is written two times

parts.note: E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Hitting the same spot on the chin twice, like a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: A compass point (E) is used twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatee is a small pointed beard grown on the chin.

clue.text: Kitchen heater tested in couple's absence

indicators.note: with the couple absent, their letters leave the word for tested

parts.note: something tested has been proven
PR is short for pair, a couple

explanation.surface: A cooker is tried out while the pair living there are away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absence' removes PR (pair) from PROVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is the enclosed cooking appliance that heats food in a kitchen.

clue.text: Nothing stops rioting in US coastal city

indicators.note: nothing stops the rioting by plugging a gap in it
rioting suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Nothing halts the unrest in an American seaside city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' rearranges US COASTAL and 'stops' puts O inside. The surface calls it coastal, but it is inland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscaloosa is a city in Alabama, home of the University of Alabama.

clue.text: Port road morning mist envelops

indicators.note: the mist wraps around the road, holding it inside

parts.note: steam is a mist of vapour

explanation.surface: A road in a harbour town shrouded in early mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'envelops' wraps the mist round the road; the morning is written first although the clue gives it second.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the Dutch capital and a major seaport.

clue.text: Guy following drunk's perilous route

indicators.note: the guy comes after the drunk

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a guy is a rope that steadies a tent

explanation.surface: A man trails after a drunk on a dangerous way home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'drunk' means 'is'. 'Guy' reads as a man but is a tent rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A high wire walked by acrobats is a dangerous path to cross.

clue.text: Scotsman involved with extremely datable woman

indicators.note: the Scot is wrapped up in the letters, as one is involved in an affair
extremely takes only the outermost letters of the word after it

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot goes out with someone very attractive to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes D and E from 'datable'; 'involved with' puts IAN between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Diane is a female given name, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Irritation right inside retina needing treatment

indicators.note: inside places the word for right within the rearranged letters
something needing treatment is to be worked on, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: 'yes' and 'right!' both express agreement

explanation.surface: A sore spot on the retina that needs medical attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing treatment' makes ETRAIN; 'inside' holds the agreeing word within it. 'right' as an exclamation means yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is the soreness and fatigue of overworked eyes, an irritation.

clue.text: More than reasonable fare to Jupiter or Mars?

definitions.text: More than reasonable fare to Jupiter or Mars?

parts.words: More than reasonable fare to Jupiter or Mars?
parts.note: fare reads as a ticket price to the planets, but means food: the divine dish of the gods named, far better than reasonable

explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' and the planets suggest the cost of space travel; Jupiter and Mars are really Roman gods, and fare is their food.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth this is the food of the gods that grants immortality, far above ordinary meals.

clue.text: Remaining quietly hidden takes trouble and effort

parts.note: to dog someone is to trouble or plague them
a go is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: Staying silently out of sight takes a lot of bother and work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie doggo' is British slang for staying still and out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggo is informal British slang for keeping quiet and hidden, as in lying low.

clue.text: Whitish individual tours China and India

indicators.note: the individual goes round the others, as a tourist goes round a country

parts.note: an individual is one
china is cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), a pal
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A pale person travels round China and India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' has the individual go round the others. 'China' is cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline describes the milky, pale, cloudy colour of opal.

clue.text: Shoot at stoat going round at rear of building

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter
the stoat goes round the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: Fire at a weasel-like animal running round behind a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' has the stoat enclose 'at'; 'rear of' takes the last letter of 'building'. 'Shoot' means sprout, not fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot is to send out new growth, as a seed does when it sprouts.

clue.text: Stadium beside lake accommodates second team

indicators.note: the lake is placed alongside the stadium
the stadium and lake together take in the second, giving it room

parts.note: a stadium is an arena

explanation.surface: A ground by the water houses a reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodates' puts S inside ARENA + L, and 'beside' puts L after ARENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous London football club, so it names a team.

clue.text: Convert smallest amount for vegetable

parts.note: to convert something is to turn it into something else
1p, one penny, is the smallest British coin, with the figure read as I

explanation.surface: Change a tiny sum into a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 1p (one penny) is the lowest British coin; the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root vegetable with white flesh.

clue.text: Stay with drinker for meal before suffering

parts.note: to last is to stay or endure
to sup is to drink, so a drinker is one who sups

explanation.surface: Hang on with a drinker for one more meal before you feel bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' is Christ's Passion: the Last Supper came just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Supper was the meal Jesus shared with his disciples just before his Passion.

clue.text: Notice me preparing small silver tray for starters

indicators.note: for starters takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Pay attention to me getting a little silver platter ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' takes the first letters of 'preparing small silver tray'.
explanation.definitionFit: The whispered sound used to catch someone's attention discreetly.

clue.text: Old Cretan at home tucking into grouse

indicators.note: the phrase for at home is pushed inside the complaint

parts.note: to grouse is to moan or complain
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: An ancient islander, sitting at home, eats a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the bird but is a complaint; 'tucking into' reads as eating, but signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minoans were the Bronze Age civilisation of Crete.

clue.text: Badge one gains in manoeuvres

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: manoeuvres are movements, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A soldier earns a decoration on military exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges GAINS IN into NSIGNIA after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia is a badge or emblem of rank or office.

clue.text: Monk secures poor grade in spelling competition

indicators.note: secures holds the grade inside the competition

parts.note: a spelling bee is a contest of spelling
D is a low exam grade

explanation.surface: A monk gets a bad mark in a spelling contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' puts D inside BEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was the eighth-century English monk and historian.

clue.text: Introducing hard line, write rubbish about athletic contest

indicators.note: introducing puts the first pair of letters into the rest

parts.note: to pen is to write
tat is cheap rubbish
on means about, concerning
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A sports writer, toeing a firm line, writes nonsense about an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introducing' puts the hard and line abbreviations into the rest; H for hard is the pencil grade.
explanation.definitionFit: The pentathlon is an athletics competition of five events.
